proposed_core_edits.reason: The finite exposure, realized-outcome, and known propensity coordinates must be explicitly induced by the common assignment-independent joint cylinder maps; this makes the exact interior coupling and primitive-coordinate influence calculation follow from the corrected locality premise.

prose_updates.tldr: Two conditionally independent assignment waves on one no-carryover schedule identify the Palm population covariance through observable cross-wave IPW products. A joint assignment--innovation cylinder version, common to every assignment outside one null set, now also explicitly induces every finite exposure, outcome, propensity, and score coordinate on the buffered interior. These primitives give order-\(n^{-1}\) centering bias and root-\(n\) finite-sample concentration, size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic. A verified four-cell local schedule has common support at the level of the complete buffered graph--assignment--exposure--outcome record and proves a matching full-observation minimax lower bound. Thus, for distinct focal labels, both the full-observation and score-vector separation radii are \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) for fixed \(r,B,\varepsilon,\alpha,\beta\), \(p=1/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta<1\).

project_justification.gap: Janson2015 classifies the zero-long-run-variance boundary for finite block factors, while one-wave interference papers study effect or estimator-variance inference. Viviano2020 develops a two-wave network design in which a pilot estimates variance and the second wave optimizes participation and treatment; these results do not supply a repeated-randomization test of the Palm population-covariance boundary or a full-observation minimax converse for it.
project_justification.niche: Conditional replication removes assignment noise from cross-wave IPW products. The joint assignment--innovation cylinder condition supplies one version simultaneously over all assignment cells, and the buffered restriction uses that same map to induce the finite exposure, outcome, and propensity coordinates. This common local rule yields stationarity and deterministic primitive influence, while four local assignment cells leave unobserved schedule coordinates after two waves and give common support to the induced observed-data laws needed for a full-record information bound.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the cross-wave identity, order-\(n^{-1}\) centering control, root-\(n\) concentration, finite-sample size and power, and an exactly unbiased lag-separated statistic under the corrected common local versions. For distinct focal exposure labels, it also constructs a causal-realizable four-cell submodel with \(\operatorname{KL}\le2N_nt^2\) for the complete declared record and linearly changing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), yielding matching \(\Theta(n^{-1/2})\) minimax rates for the full observation and its score-vector subexperiment.

sampling_model.design: Two conditionally independent Bernoulli assignment waves with known probability \(p\) are applied to the same graph, exposure mapping, and no-carryover potential-outcome schedule after a prespecified washout; the covariance cutoff and analysis interior are fixed before assignment.
sampling_model.units: The canonical specialization observes \(\Lambda_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and analyzes \(I_n=\{r+1,\ldots,n-r\}\). Outside one law-null set independent of assignment, a joint radius-\(r\) Borel cylinder map represents every exposure--outcome assignment cell. On the buffered interior, the finite exposure, realized-outcome, propensity, and score coordinates are explicitly induced by that same map and the restricted primitive coordinates.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary assignments in each wave generate local exposure labels and realized outcomes under one common shift-equivariant schedule; the left shift satisfies \((\theta^kd)_j=d_{j+k}\) and \(\{i,j\}\in\theta^kG\) if and only if \(\{i+k,j+k\}\in G\). The full minimax observation contains the finite graph, both assignments, both exposure arrays, both realized-outcome arrays, and known propensity coordinates.
sampling_model.overlap: Both focal exposures have conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\) in each wave, so every IPW division in both the infinite and explicitly restricted finite scores is well defined.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Propensities are known from the Bernoulli design and are computed on the buffered interior from the same local exposure cylinder. The mean-centered statistic estimates only the two wave means; the lag-separated statistic removes that centering bias exactly. Neither procedure estimates unit-specific conditional scores or fits a regression.

prose_updates.related_work: Janson2015 supplies the finite-block coboundary result used to interpret the zero boundary, but no two-wave statistic or testing experiment. Leung2022ANI supplies one-wave exposure-IPW and approximate-neighborhood-interference analysis; no ANI or graph-HAC transfer is used here. AronowSamii2017 supplies exposure mappings and known design propensities. Viviano2020 is the closest design comparator: it uses a first-wave pilot to estimate variance and optimizes second-wave participation and treatment for average treatment and spillover effects. The present work does not claim that two-wave network designs are new; it uses conditionally independent replications with common joint local versions to identify and test a Palm covariance boundary and proves a full-observation common-support minimax converse. LiWager2022 and FanLengWu2025 target causal-effect estimation and estimator variance under graphon models. Tsybakov2009 supplies the classical Pinsker and two-point testing inequalities used after the new four-cell likelihood calculation.
prose_updates.interpretation: The null \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) is a covariance-cancellation boundary, not a claim that conditional exposure effects are homogeneous. On the line, the joint cylinder condition makes the conditional score a finite block factor, so Janson's result represents the null score as a finite-block coboundary. Rejection certifies positive Palm population variation; failure to reject only places that variation within the stated finite-sample threshold.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The design requires two conditionally independent assignment waves applied to one no-carryover schedule and one common joint assignment--innovation cylinder version. The full-observation converse includes the observed finite graph, assignments, exposures, realized outcomes, and known propensities, but not the innovations or unobserved assignment-cell outcomes. The graph extension requires a single bounded local score map shared by all sites and waves, a fixed footprint, and deterministic covariance-support sets on F\o lner interiors. No growing bandwidth, random shortest-path cutoff, approximate-neighborhood-interference transfer, endogenous graph-distance HAC, annealed CLT or Wald theorem, or BondEtAl2012 reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The target is \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\), the long-run covariance sum of local conditional exposure-effect scores under the Palm law. The interval results and their finitely generated amenable Cayley-graph extension use a fixed deterministic local cutoff, bounded outcomes, overlap, two conditionally independent waves, common assignment--innovation cylinder versions, bounded primitive influence, and bounded score dependence. The finite interval record is coupled by explicitly inducing its exposure, outcome, propensity, and score coordinates from those same local maps. For distinct focal labels, minimax sharpness holds for the explicitly encoded finite observed-data vector at \(p=1/2\) and \(\alpha+\beta<1\); the score-vector theorem is a corollary. The note claims neither novelty of two-wave designs nor validity for observations revealing innovations or unobserved potential outcomes.

statement_notes.justification: The exact interior coupling is derived from one assignment-independent local cylinder version, and the finite exposure, outcome, and propensity coordinates are now explicitly induced by that same version.
statement_notes.gap: BaryshnikovYukich2005 studies stabilizing finite-volume scores, while this proposition records exact boundary deletion for two repeated exposure experiments under a common local version.
statement_notes.consumer: An experimenter can implement the diagnostic after dropping a prespecified fixed-width endpoint buffer and computing all retained coordinates from the declared local rule.

statement_notes.justification: The decomposition retains the assignment--environment split and supplies the common envelope required for both concentration statistics.
statement_notes.gap: AbadieAtheyImbensWooldridge2020 separates sampling and design uncertainty without repeated local exposure-IPW scores; Leung2022ANI works conditionally on one realized finite population.
statement_notes.consumer: The split identifies which cross-wave products eliminate assignment noise and which envelope controls finite-sample error.

statement_notes.justification: Conditional replication converts the latent population covariance into an observable cross-wave moment without estimating \(m_i\).
statement_notes.gap: AronowSamii2017 identifies exposure means within one randomization, while this lemma identifies the population covariance component by two conditionally independent waves.
statement_notes.consumer: The identity lets a platform estimate graph-to-graph exposure-effect variation using only recorded assignments, exposures, outcomes, and known propensities.

statement_notes.justification: This specialization interprets the diagnostic null as the published finite-block coboundary boundary rather than as causal homogeneity.
statement_notes.gap: Janson2015, Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 1 establish the finite-dependent coboundary and endpoint laws; this proposition verifies their hypotheses for the declared local score.
statement_notes.consumer: A researcher who fails to reject can report the correct boundary interpretation without claiming that unit-level exposure effects are constant.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem turns the uniform concentration map into a nonasymptotic level guarantee and an explicit root-sample-size power separation, including the non-strict boundary \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)\).
statement_notes.gap: Leung2022ANI gives one-assignment network-HAC inference, and FanLengWu2025 gives graphon-based variance inference; neither tests a Palm exposure-score covariance by repeated assignments.
statement_notes.consumer: A platform with two washout-separated waves can test whether the Palm population component is detectably positive.

statement_notes.justification: A cross-wave product at lag \(2r+1\) estimates \(\tau_{\mathrm P}^2\) exactly, so subtracting it removes sample-centering bias without estimating another nuisance.
statement_notes.gap: The sample-mean-centered statistic has a uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) bias allowance; this proposition gives an exact finite-sample expectation identity and a directly usable bias-free threshold.
statement_notes.consumer: Practitioners with two independent waves can use the displayed statistic as a robustness diagnostic alongside the mean-centered headline test.

statement_notes.justification: A causal-realizable four-cell schedule satisfies the corrected \(\Psi_i\)-cylinder condition with an empty exceptional set and gives a common-support likelihood bound for every Borel test of the complete declared record.
statement_notes.gap: Viviano2020 optimizes a second-wave design after a pilot; it does not prove a full-observation information lower bound for testing the Palm covariance boundary.
statement_notes.consumer: A designer can use the finite-sample upper threshold knowing that no common Borel test of the declared full observation improves its separation order uniformly over the class.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem derives identification, finite-volume centering bias, and root-volume concentration from one common bounded site- and wave-independent local score rule, rather than assuming stationarity or a limit law.
statement_notes.gap: Existing interference results do not provide this fixed-footprint repeated-randomization Palm covariance diagnostic on deterministic F\o lner interiors.
statement_notes.consumer: The integer-line theorem is the specialization with a fixed radius footprint; other finitely generated amenable Cayley graphs use the same explicit estimator after replacing interval interiors by footprint interiors.
